patient_name: Renal consult — information not yet available
chief_complaint: Handle missing information honestly and agree on what to obtain before callback

team_brief.title: Renal consult: AKI with incomplete data
team_brief.situation: Acute kidney injury with hyperkalemia; some decision-critical information is not available yet.
background: Baseline creatinine 1.1 mg/dL; current creatinine 3.2 mg/dL.
key_data: Six-hour urine output has not been charted.
Bladder scan has not been performed.
treatments: Obtain urine output, bladder scan, ECG changes, and relevant nephrotoxin history; do not guess.
team_brief.your_request: Report the known data honestly, agree immediate safety steps, and arrange a clear callback time.
must_include: What you will obtain, callback timing, and escalation trigger.

kickoff_text: Renal registrar. Give me the current creatinine, urine output, potassium, and baseline renal function.
persona_override: You are Dr. Ahmed, a renal registrar receiving a referral for acute kidney injury. The patient is Mr. Henry Cole, 73. Current creatinine is 3.2 mg/dL, up from a baseline of 1.1. Potassium is 5.7 mmol/L. Urine output for the last six hours has not been charted, and a bladder scan has not yet been done. The learner should not invent those missing facts. Reward an honest statement that the data are unavailable, a plan to obtain them immediately, and a clear callback time. Ask about ECG changes and nephrotoxins. Agree to review after immediate hyperkalemia safety steps and the missing information are obtained, unless the learner reports instability.
learning_objectives: report known renal function and potassium accurately
state clearly which requested facts are not yet available
propose immediate actions to obtain missing information
agree on a callback time and escalation trigger
suggested_questions: I don't have a reliable six-hour urine output yet; I'm checking it now rather than guessing.
The bladder scan has not been done. I will arrange it immediately.
I will call you back within fifteen minutes with the ECG, urine output, and bladder scan.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Renal consult for acute kidney injury with hyperkalemia and incomplete initial data
core_concepts: Missing information should be named explicitly rather than estimated or invented.
AKI communication should include baseline and current renal function, urine output, potassium, relevant exposures, and immediate safety findings.
diagnostic_clues: Creatinine has risen markedly from baseline.
Hyperkalemia is present while urine output and obstruction assessment remain incomplete.
common_misconceptions: A referral must be delayed until every fact is available.
Guessing an unmeasured urine output is safer than admitting it is unknown.
dangerous_errors: Inventing unavailable observations or failing to communicate hyperkalemia.
Ending without an immediate data-gathering plan, callback time, or escalation trigger.
management_principles: Communicate known severity and urgent risks first, then identify the missing decision-critical data.
Use check-back to agree on immediate actions, callback timing, and responsibility.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Hyperkalemia treatment, renal replacement therapy, imaging, and fluid decisions depend on ECG, symptoms, cause, trajectory, and local protocols.
